adverse_F03_verbatim.topic: Last commutator in the claimed six-term source identity is reversed
adverse_F03_verbatim.detail: With alpha=nabla_mu F_nu and beta=nabla_nu F_mu, the source's last term is -i eta^2[alpha,beta]. B writes -i eta^2[beta,alpha], which is its negative. The first five terms agree in coefficient, sign and commutator order with printed (94). There is no simultaneous orientation change of the entire plaquette expression in B that would justify reversing this term alone. Consequently the statement that (4) reads exactly as source (94) is false, even after the separate product-rule correction.
adverse_F03_verbatim.exact_witness: At U0=I take F_mu(x)=F_nu(x)=0, alpha=t sigma_x and beta=t sigma_y. All first five terms vanish. Source (94) gives 2 eta^2 t^2 sigma_z, while B gives -2 eta^2 t^2 sigma_z. A nonzero t can be chosen arbitrarily small to fit the local field/jet domain. An exact SymPy Pauli calculation reproduced these opposite matrices.

findings.topic: Actual fixed-root transported fields and S=eta d0F
findings.detail: Set p=(x,y,z,w), y=x+eta e_mu and w=x+eta e_nu. At the same fixed base point x, the oriented fields along (x,y),(y,z),(z,w),(w,x) are X, R(U0(x,y))F_nu(y)=Y+eta alpha, -R(U0(x,w))F_mu(w)=-X-eta beta, -Y. Thus C uses the actual covariant fields, not untransported differences. Their sum is eta(alpha-beta)=eta d0F by source (3.4). The (34) order (z,w),(w,x),(x,y),(y,z) is the two-edge cyclic rotation of this same list. No flat-background assumption or new transport path is required. The comparison is at a common base point; it does not authorize arbitrary spatial-root or transport changes.

findings.topic: Cyclic-prefix invariance has precisely scalar scope
findings.detail: For any prefix sum P and total sum S, moving that prefix behind the remaining fields gives Q(rotated a)-Q(a)=-2i[P,S]. Since Tr(S[P,S])=Tr(SPS-S^2P)=0 by trace cyclicity, (1/2)Tr(d0F Q) is invariant when S=eta d0F. All three nontrivial prefix rotations were also checked by exact cyclic-word reduction. The common-root matrix-valued Q generally changes; C explicitly declines to equate those matrices. The initially inherited wording describing C_p as the original ordered sum is qualified by the later explicit representative and scalar-only statement, and does not require a false matrix equality. Fixed-background complex bilinear trace has the same cyclic identity.

findings.topic: B error remains a matrix error although its scalar contribution vanishes
findings.detail: Q_B-Q_C=2i eta^2[alpha,beta] is not identically zero. B report F03 and its exact Pauli witness remain adverse for B. However (1/2)Tr((d0F)(Q_B-Q_C))=i eta^2 Tr((alpha-beta)[alpha,beta])=0 as an identity for arbitrary complex matrices. Each of Tr(alpha[alpha,beta]) and Tr(beta[alpha,beta]) vanishes by cyclicity. Consequently the correction fixes the claimed matrix identity without altering this scalar cubic action. It does not retroactively validate B or claim the uncontracted expressions are interchangeable.

findings.topic: First and second variations remain consistent after correction
findings.detail: Both the cyclic-root difference and B-to-C scalar difference vanish identically as cubic functions on the fixed-U0 linear field coordinates, not only at one chosen F. Their first and second Frechet variations therefore vanish. Independent exact expansion at F+t u+s v verified the zero scalar polynomial and its coefficients of t and ts for each difference. With Q(F,v) the symmetric polarization, delta Q(F,F)[v]=2Q(F,v). Direct variation gives G3=(1/2)d0sharp Q(F,F)+Q_Fsharp d0F and K3(F)v=d0sharp Q(F,v)+Q_vsharp d0F+Q_Fsharp d0v, exactly C equation (5). In bilinear form the Hessian is <d0u,Q(F,v)>+<d0v,Q(F,u)>+<d0F,Q(u,v)>. The three combined terms are invariant; individual matrix terms or their adjoints need not coincide across representatives. No derivative of a field-dependent transport is omitted because U0 is fixed.
